statement: The stem-and-leaf plot shows the ages of the $12$ volunteers at a park cleanup. In the plot, $1 \mid 6$ represents $16$ years. $$\begin{array}{r|l} \text{Stem} & \text{Leaf} \\ \hline 1 & 6\ \ 8\ \ 9 \\ 2 & 0\ \ 3\ \ 3\ \ 7 \\ 3 & 1\ \ 4\ \ 8 \\ 4 & 2\ \ 5 \end{array}$$ How many of the volunteers are at least $23$ years old?

choices.misconception: I read at least 23 as older than 23, so I left out both volunteers who are exactly 23.
I counted the leaf 3 in the 2 row only once, but there are two volunteers who are 23.
I counted every age in the 2 row, including 20, along with all the ages in the 3 and 4 rows.

hints: Each leaf is one volunteer. Read $2 \mid 3$ as $23$.
At least $23$ means $23$ or older. Count the qualifying leaves row by row.
In the $2$ row, the ages $23$, $23$ and $27$ count. Then add every leaf in the $3$ and $4$ rows.

solutions.reliable: The ages that are $23$ or more are $23$, $23$, $27$ from the $2$ row, $31$, $34$, $38$ from the $3$ row and $42$, $45$ from the $4$ row. That is $3 + 3 + 2 = 8$ volunteers.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
